definitions.baselines: std = prior season-to-date mean PTS (primary); l10 = last <=10 prior games
definitions.events: x125/x150/x200: PTS >= 1.25/1.5/2.0 x baseline; p5/p10: >= baseline + 5/10; z15: (PTS - baseline) / prior SD >= 1.5
definitions.eligibility: >=5 min played, >=5 prior games this season and overall, opponent with >=5 prior games
definitions.thin: a cell or level with < 30 players or < 300 player-games is thin: shown, never ranked; top25 and top10 are always thin (25 / 10 players)
definitions.lens_B: same game: describes how the night happened, NOT predictive

insights.title: Usage-vacuum chip on tonight's game / player card
insights.text: When regular teammates averaging 20+ PPG together are out, a player's 1.5x big-night rate is 22.2% vs 11.4% (adjusted +6.6 pp [+5.5, +7.7]); +10 11.3% vs 5.5%. Show it only from the inactive list (about 30 minutes before tip), wording 'associated with'. Hide it for 2026-27-only views until there are more events.

insights.title: Say 'no bounce-back' plainly
insights.text: There is no bounce-back: after a weak last game the raw 1.5x rate is lower (RR 0.86 [0.82, 0.91]) and the adjusted odds ratio is 0.94 [0.87, 1.01] (no credible change); after two weak games the adjusted +10 odds are lower (OR 0.77). Stars show no weak-game or hot-game dependence at all. Do not present rebound-game or hot-streak chips as signals.

insights.title: Relabel hot-game / minutes-up as 'average is stale'
insights.text: The hot-game effect (RR 1.42 [1.35, 1.50]) collapses against the last-10 baseline (RR 1.08 [1.03, 1.14]). Offer a baseline toggle (season-to-date vs last 10) on any big-night chip and note that recent form is already in the last-10 number.

insights.title: Defence and pace tiers: small, with CIs, not 'stars feast on bad defences'
insights.text: Adjusted, bottom-10 defences add about +1.1 pp to 1.5x and top-10 defences take away -1.4 pp; fast opponents add +1.4 pp. The top-50 effect against bottom-10 defences is not credible (adjusted OR 1.00 [0.84, 1.20]) and unstable by season. Elite defences are the more reliable signal (fewer big nights).

insights.title: 'What does not matter' strip
insights.text: Once the other factors are held fixed, home vs away, back-to-back and rest days, the opponent's recent defensive form, the opponent missing players, NBA Cup games and late season have no credible big-night effect (raw second-night and late-season lifts of +1.4 and +3.4 pp for 1.5x disappear after adjustment). A short 'tested, nothing there' list is a useful honest panel.

insights.title: 'Role change in progress' flag
insights.text: Recent promotion to the starting five or last-5 minutes 3+ above the season average are associated with +2.5 to +3 pp of 1.5x big nights against the season-to-date baseline (not against the last-10 baseline): show as context for a player whose average is out of date, not as a forecast.

insights.title: Stars vs everyone toggle
insights.text: Top-50 players reach 1.5x 8.5% of games vs 17.7% for others but +10 10.7% vs 7.4%: say which definition. Defence-tier lifts and the 1.5x vacuum lift are the same ratio for both groups (the +10 vacuum ratio is smaller for stars, the +6 pp effect is the same); recent-form effects (hot game, weak game) exist for non-stars only.

insights.title: 'How the night happened' bar on recaps (same game, labelled)
insights.text: For a big night show minutes / shots per minute / efficiency shares of the excess (all players about 28% / 36% / 35%; top 50 about 18% / 44% / 38%), plus extra minutes, FGA and TS% vs the player's norm. Label it 'how it happened, not a prediction'.

insights.title: Do not ship a pregame big-night probability
insights.text: Pregame AUC is 0.70 (1.5x) and 0.65 (+10), only 0.04 and 0.12 above a controls-only model; for top-50 stars the pregame factors add nothing credible for 1.5x. Show base rates by context bucket (prior-average tier x teammates-out) instead of a model score.

insights.title: Per-player big-night cards: credible cases only, with the chance count
insights.text: Show a player-specific big-night pattern only if the shrunk interval excludes the league mean, and print 'expected by chance' beside the count (20 players at |z| >= 2.5 vs 3.8 expected for 1.5x). No top-25 star qualifies; the credible ones are mostly role players (e.g. OG Anunoby, Deni Avdija, Payton Pritchard at 1.5x). Hide player flags for 2026-27.

insights.title: Mark 2026-27 provisional and hide thin cells
insights.text: 2026-27 has about 106 1.5x events so far (std baseline, 8+ PPG); top 25 / top 10 are always thin (25 / 10 players): show counts only, never a ranking.

caveats: Associational, not causal. Teammates out is a context variable, not a randomised condition: teams that lose scorers also change minutes, lineups and opponents' game plans.

The baseline matters. Season-to-date averages lag role changes, so 'hot last game', 'minutes up' and 'promoted' look like effects against the std baseline and mostly vanish against the l10 baseline. The prior average is also noisy early in a season (the early-season adjusted effect of about +2.6 pp for 1.5x partly reflects that).

Out is observed from the box score (inactive list or non-coach DNP) of the game itself. It is knowable at about tip-off but not days ahead; late scratches and game-time decisions are not separated, and a coach's-decision DNP is not counted.
The 5-minute rule uses same-game minutes: players who play under 5 minutes are not in the denominator (they cannot have big nights).
Segments use train-period PPG ranks, so top-N membership has no look-ahead but includes players who later changed role. Top 25 and top 10 have 25 and 10 players: always thin, descriptive only.

2026-27 is provisional (through Nov 9: ~106 1.5x events and few games per player once the 5-prior-game and opponent cold-start rules are applied). Pooled spans that include it carry the provisional flag.
Lens B is an accounting identity with the points total: its lifts and the same-game model's AUC of 0.99 are not evidence of anything predictive.

Not available: defender matchups, referee crews, betting lines and totals (the combined score is same-game), the pregame injury report (only the inactive list), shot quality or tracking data, play-by-play (so no 'minute of foul trouble').

Multiple comparisons: about 50 factor levels x 6 cuts x 30 cells in the mart. Use the adjusted columns and the stability table, not single cells; interaction and per-player flags are reported with expected-by-chance counts.

Logistic fits use player-clustered covariance; a few rare-event cells hit convergence warnings (the fits fall back to BFGS); cells that could not be fitted are logged in the manifest and left empty, never filled.
